decision_reason: RattleSNP is a reusable Snakemake mapping/SNP-calling pipeline with user documentation and a versioned 1.1.0 distribution. CIRAD’s cluster software list identifies and distributes version 1.1.0, and a peer-reviewed study documents exact RattleSNP use. The direct source contains an eligible GPL-3.0-or-later grant; catalog the GPL option, not the additional CeCILL-C claim.

government_provenance.note: The project description identifies Sébastien Ravel (CIRAD) and says intellectual property belongs to CIRAD and the authors; the source is maintained in the PHIM/sravel IRD Forge namespace. CIRAD’s own FAQ identifies it as a French public EPIC under two ministries: https://www.cirad.fr/foire-aux-questions.

public_source.note: The Forge project is publicly accessible and presents the functional Snakemake pipeline. A source distribution is also published on PyPI; the direct root LICENCE is visible at https://forge.ird.fr/phim/sravel/RattleSNP/-/blob/master/LICENCE.

eligible_license.note: The direct root license identifies GNU GPL v3.0 or later; GitLab labels the project accordingly. The README/PyPI description also mentions CeCILL-C, but this decision relies only on the eligible GPL option. The pass covers RattleSNP-authored code, not third-party tools such as BWA/GATK.

primary_evidence.note: CIRAD’s AGAP cluster software inventory lists RattleSNP 1.1.0 as installed and describes its mapping/SNP-calling and reporting functions. A peer-reviewed paper also says the exact tool was used to process sequencing data: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9732276/. User documentation describes mapping, SNP calling, and configurable workflows: https://rattlesnp.readthedocs.io/en/latest/ABOUT.html.

product_identity: RattleSNP, a Snakemake pipeline for sequence mapping, SNP calling, and filtering/report generation
agency: CIRAD, UMR PHIM; authored by Sébastien Ravel (CIRAD)
license: GPL-3.0-or-later (direct root grant; README also mentions CeCILL-C, which is not relied on)
family_note: Standalone bioinformatics workflow; third-party tools invoked by the workflow retain their own licenses and are not included in the GPL scope assertion.
status_note: The Forge project page gives a creation date of 2022-03-15; the project’s functional code and root GPL license are available in the public repository. Older imported commit/tag timestamps are not used to backdate the current Forge publication. PyPI lists 1.0.0 in Jan 2022 and 1.1.0 in Feb 2023; 1.1.0 is the release currently corroborated by CIRAD’s cluster software inventory. Repository activity continued through 2025-03, within the 24-month freshness window at review time.

decision_reason: Snakecdysis is a standalone, agency-authored Snakemake workflow packaging tool, not merely a generated template: it provides a Python package and CLI to scaffold, package, and run Snakemake workflows. It has a versioned PyPI source distribution (2.0.1) and user/install documentation. The direct MIT grant provides an OSI-approved license option despite separate CeCILL-C labeling.

government_provenance.note: The exact package record identifies Sébastien Ravel (CIRAD) as maintainer and states that intellectual property belongs to CIRAD and the authors. CIRAD identifies itself as a French public EPIC under ministerial supervision: https://www.cirad.fr/foire-aux-questions.

public_source.note: The public IRD Forge repository exposes the project, releases, README, license, and changelog. PyPI distributes a public source tarball for version 2.0.1: https://pypi.org/project/snakecdysis/.

eligible_license.note: The 0.0.1 source release contains the full MIT grant; PyPI’s current license expression is MIT. The project description also mentions CeCILL-C, but the decision relies only on the MIT grant and applies to Snakecdysis-authored source, not workflows or external dependencies packaged by its users.

primary_evidence.note: PyPI shows stable versioned releases through 2.0.1 (2025-04-03), source distributions, and installation via pip. The maintained manual explains how to scaffold and package a workflow with the generate_template command and provides package/install instructions: https://snakecdysis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/package.html.

product_identity: Snakecdysis, a reusable Python package and CLI for scaffolding and packaging Snakemake workflows
agency: CIRAD, UMR PHIM; authored and maintained by Sébastien Ravel (CIRAD)
license: MIT (eligible direct grant; project description also mentions CeCILL-C)
family_note: Independent workflow-packaging tool, distinct from the example workflows it scaffolds or packages.
status_note: The license-bearing commit adds the MIT grant on 2023-02-16; first PyPI version 0.0.1 was released the same day. The current release is 2.0.1 (2025-04-03); documentation provides concrete commands and packaging steps. CIRAD public-body status: https://www.cirad.fr/foire-aux-questions.

decision_reason: This repository is a mixed collection of documentation/data and accessory scripts for one research group’s Grist instance, not an independently notable software product. Grist is the operational application; this repository organizes resources for that instance and does not establish a separately distributed application or reusable tool with its own user/install pathway.

government_provenance.note: The exact README describes the repository as the XPLAIN group’s resource repository for its Grist instance and identifies the PHIM/IRD context. IRD is a French public EPST: https://www.ird.fr/lird-presentation-et-historique.

public_source.note: The repository is public and exposes source materials, including accessory code, notebooks, documentation, and Grist resources.

eligible_license.note: The root MIT grant is an eligible code license, but the repository mixes software with data, documentation, and other resources; the blanket scope across non-code assets was not established. This does not change the product-scope rejection.

primary_evidence.note: The README frames this as accessory material for the group’s single Grist database instance, with deployment setup kept in a separate private repository. No independent product identity, versioned release plus standalone user/install guidance, independent reuse, or distinct production application was established.

product_identity: XPLAIN Grist instance accessory repository (documentation, data, notebooks, and scripts), not a distinct software product
agency: IRD/UMR PHIM, XPLAIN research group (repository context; no standalone product sponsorship established)
license: MIT for code per root grant; scope over bundled data/documentation unresolved
family_note: Do not duplicate Grist itself as software; this is an accessory repository for one instance. The repository mentions a sample-tracker Dash app, but no independently distributed or separately notable product was established.
status_note: Rejected on product identity, not because the repository is private. IRD Forge page and project README are primary sources; issue discussions and docs concern the XPLAIN team’s single Grist instance. Clearance path: demonstrate a separate operational application with install/use documentation or independent reuse, and clarify license scope for non-code material.

decision_reason: The assigned repository is not publicly inspectable: the project URL redirects to IRD Forge sign-in and the unauthenticated project API lookup returns not found. A public source is required for admission. The title and metadata license are leads only; I could not verify whether the repository contains software, a dataset, or the claimed rights notice.

government_provenance.note: The URL is in the TransVIHMI/IRD namespace, but the inaccessible project body provides no inspectable product-specific sponsor, owner, or steward relationship.

public_source.note: The project redirects to a sign-in page rather than exposing source without credentials; the corresponding unauthenticated project API path is not found. Public-source eligibility therefore fails.

eligible_license.note: The source inventory’s CC-BY-ND-4.0 claim is not direct evidence of an OSI-approved software grant, but because the repository cannot be inspected and may be data rather than software, exact material and rights scope remain unknown.

primary_evidence.note: No project description, usable distribution, installation/user guidance, or product-specific use evidence is available without authentication.

product_identity: Unverified lead titled Clade-I Mpox virus genomic diversity DRC; repository contents not publicly inspectable
license: Unverified source metadata says CC-BY-ND-4.0; no direct software grant inspected
family_note: Do not infer source code, software identity, or license from the repository title or neighboring Mpox research projects.
status_note: Rejected because public source access failed. Metadata labels are not treated as four-check evidence. Reopen only if the project becomes publicly accessible or an official public successor/archive is provided.

decision_reason: GeVarLi is a standalone Snakemake genomic-analysis workflow developed for the AFROSCREEN public-health research program, with public code, a direct AGPL-3.0 grant, current maintenance, and detailed installation/use documentation. An official AFROSCREEN webinar presents this exact pipeline and its workflow results; later program research documents deployment across partner labs.

government_provenance.note: The exact AFROSCREEN page says GeVarLi was developed for the program and presented by Nicolas Fernandez, a bioinformatics engineer at UMI 233 TransVIHMI IRD. IRD’s official profile identifies it as a French public EPST under ministerial supervision: https://www.ird.fr/lird-presentation-et-historique.

public_source.note: The exact GitLab repository is public and has functional Snakemake workflow source. Its root LICENSE explicitly identifies GNU AGPL v3.0: https://forge.ird.fr/transvihmi/nfernandez/gevarli/-/blob/5773d33eb6a1977420e6691949403d752ddeef66/LICENSE.

eligible_license.note: The direct root grant is GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0); no conflicting source-level license was found for the workflow code. This pass is for project-authored pipeline code only; third-party tools, reference datasets/genomes, and any bundled research data retain their own terms and are not claimed to be relicensed by the root grant.

primary_evidence.note: The official program webinar describes GeVarLi by name as a public-health tool developed for AFROSCREEN and covers installation, use, and results. The current manual has explicit installation and usage sections: https://transvihmi.pages.ird.fr/nfernandez/GeVarLi/en/pages/installations/ and https://transvihmi.pages.ird.fr/nfernandez/GeVarLi/en/pages/usage/. A peer-reviewed 2026 AFROSCREEN paper says GeVarLi was deployed across partner laboratories: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13132006/.

product_identity: GeVarLi (Genome assembly, Variant calling and Lineage assignation), a standalone Snakemake workflow for SARS-CoV-2 and other emerging-virus analysis
agency: Institut de recherche pour le développement (IRD), UMI 233 TransVIHMI; developed for AFROSCREEN
geography: France; AFROSCREEN partner-laboratory use across Africa
license: AGPL-3.0 for project-authored workflow code; external tools/data retain their own terms
family_note: Product is the GeVarLi workflow repository, not the underlying sequencing data or third-party tools. Do not apply the root AGPL grant to bundled datasets or external dependencies without their own rights evidence.
status_note: The official manual says the pipeline was initially developed in 2021 for AFROSCREEN and publicly released on IRD Forge in March 2022. The repository was created 2022-03-15; the cited grant-bearing commit supplies the exact 2022 GPLv3-era source snapshot. Current repository activity is through 2026-09-22. AFROSCREEN’s 2023 webinar names the exact product and IRD engineer, while the 2026 article reports partner-laboratory deployment.
